```{r doc-code, include=FALSE}
source("../code/R/doc_code.R")
```

All panels are produced by
[`script/Figure10.R`](https://github.com/dzemmour/immgenT-cosmo-paper/blob/main/script/Figure10.R).
The code below is shown for reference (not re-executed on this page); the
images are its pre-rendered output.

Panels **10d** and **10e** both depend on Milner et al.: (d) scores that
paper's published tissue-resident memory gene signature across the atlas, and
(e) maps the cells the signature was derived from onto the reference with
T-RBI. Neither the signature nor that dataset is part of the deposited data,
and they are not reproduced here.

## Setup

```{r fig10-setup, code=code_for("../script/Figure10.R", c("^", "Load data")), eval=FALSE}
```

## (A) Trm cells on the CD8 MDE {#fig10a}

```{r fig10a-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure10.R", "10a"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig10a-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="45%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure10/10a_CD8MDE_P14_Trm_gut.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 10A.** CD8 MDE highlighting resident-memory CD8⁺ T cells mapping
predominantly to CD8.Q. Trm cells are defined here by antigen specificity and
timepoint rather than by marker expression — LCMV-specific (P14) CD8⁺ T cells
isolated from the gut 30 days after LCMV Armstrong infection — so where they
land is an independent check on the reference. Cells are coloured by immgenT
cluster.
:::

## (B) CD103⁺CD69⁺ cells across the CD8 MDE {#fig10b}

```{r fig10b-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure10.R", "10b"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig10b-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="45%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure10/10b_CD8MDE_CD103pos_CD69pos.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 10B.** CD8 MDE with CD103⁺CD69⁺ T cells in the full immgenT dataset
extending well beyond CD8.Q, indicating that canonical Trm markers do not
uniquely define this molecular state. The gating strategy is shown in (C). The
published panel renders the same 20,132 gated cells as a white-to-purple cell
density map rather than as solid points.
:::

## (C) CD69 vs CD103 by tissue {#fig10c}

```{r fig10c-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure10.R", "10c"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig10c-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="45%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c(
  "assets/Figure10/10c_CD103_CD69_small_intestine.png",
  "assets/Figure10/10c_CD103_CD69_prostate.png",
  "assets/Figure10/10c_CD103_CD69_salivary_gland.png",
  "assets/Figure10/10c_CD103_CD69_spleen.png"))
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 10C.** CD69 versus CD103 expression in memory cells from the small
intestine, prostate, salivary gland and spleen (CITE-seq, log1p(CP10K); P14
CD8⁺, 30 dpi), illustrating that canonical Trm markers are variably expressed
across tissues, including within CD8.Q — whose cells fall on both sides of the
gate. Cells are coloured by immgenT cluster.
:::

## (F) CD8.Q across organs and perturbations {#fig10f}

```{r fig10f-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure10.R", "10f"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig10f-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure10/10f_alluvial_CD8Q.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 10F.** Alluvial plot showing the contribution of CD8.Q cells (red)
across a broad range of organs and immune perturbations, illustrating CD8.Q as
a transcriptional basin into which cells from diverse biological conditions
converge. Perturbations are downsampled to 1,000 cells each so that flow width
reflects breadth of distribution rather than how many cells an experiment
contributed.
:::
